_lead: Battle gear of this age: this is the age of a luminous magic empire built on bone-silver rings, white sky towers and elemental kings bound in furnaces, so battle gear here looks like gear from a fantasy JRPG of that world, not plain medieval kit: engraved spell-rings, beast-cores and cold white spell-light on the armour and weapons. The description above already sets how much gear this character wears, from rank, wealth and taste (11-21): follow it exactly. Where it says plain, simple, unadorned or no armour, keep it that way; this note only supplies the look of the pieces it names. No electric lights, no modern clothes,
崛起上: no gunpowder and no guns of any kind; no sky towers yet. Leftover beast-age gear: highland heavy cavalry in armour pressed from copper-coloured wolf hide, scales mixed with pale silver dust that flashes cold in the charge, a seven-ringed wall brand on the chest with the inmost ring scraped off, a whole wolf pelt as cloak and the wolf head as a helm for the captains; noble retainers under house banners with silver-plumed helms; blades of beast bone and old iron set with a still-living beast-core that glows with its element, thunder-beast hides that spark; academy mages wear no armour, only grey wool robes, a bone-silver name ring and a bone-silver casting ring set into the bracer or staff head, from which fine threads of cold white light unfold and link hand to hand into a ring; the best of them carry no staff at all.
崛起下: no gunpowder and no guns of any kind. The first sky towers: inside their glow, armour, bracers and lamps carry fine white lines fed by tower light, while gear made for outside has a sealed beast-core with a visible core cap on the back, and core-set bracers throw up a three-foot shield of white light; the legion takes shape, plain grey armour under grey-blue cloaks embroidered with a ring of fire and two crossed keys, the same emblem painted on round shields, a bone-silver name ring on every hand, war-mages whose rings light up name by name as ring-sigils turn open on the ground; legion gate guards with charred gauntlets; the eastern sun kingdom fights in white plate edged with gold and gold-faced sun-wheel shields that bloom with golden light; hunters in copper wolf hide with hard bows, wolf-eared couriers in wolfskin with a brass message tube.
帝国: no gunpowder and no guns of any kind. White and bone-silver reach the armour: palace and sky-city guards in white plate engraved with a ring of fire and two crossed keys, the engraving glowing cold white, halberds sheathed in pale bone-silver; legions dressed by station, northern legionaries in grey plate under frosted bearskin cloaks worn fur-out, storm-platform legionaries whose plates hold stored lightning that crackles and lifts their hair, the southern legion in sand-coloured cloaks; blades forged in blue elemental fire with a faint blue sheen; core-set blades, sealed-core bracers and core lamps are common legion kit, later kept as heirlooms; archmages with one or two floating rings of rune-light; beast examiners with a bone-silver lamp behind clear glass; northern hunters in white fox fur worn fur-out with antler bows; dragonkin in scale-pattern armour with bone shields and a bone-silver band on the horns.
魔族之世: no gunpowder and no guns of any kind. The towers at their brightest: inside their glow the white lines and bone-silver thread on armour shine cold white by themselves; strong mages wear two or three ring-sigils on bracers and belt, the strongest have several rings of rune-light turning around them at once; idle legions in old grey plate and grey-blue cloaks whose emblem has worn white, a short sword, an heirloom core-set weapon passed down the ranks, newer armour with thinner bone-silver inlay; registry squads led by a beast examiner holding a bone-silver lamp and a clerk with a registry book; horned, scaled, winged and tailed people born into ordinary families have no war gear of their own and fight with the tools of their trade, a driver's whip, a plane, a chisel, scales serving as thin armour, a carved wooden registry tag with a burnt-in ring-sigil at the throat.
末年上: no gunpowder and no guns of any kind. The empire still glows but its crests fade: border legions turned into noble private guards, house-coloured over-robes over grey legion plate with the house arms embroidered in bone-silver thread that lights up inside the tower glow, rich houses giving their guards white plate engraved with the family crest; old legion plates whose ring-sigils have dimmed by half, empty core sockets refilled with a family's old core; retired standard-bearers in washed-out grey-blue cloaks with a faded emblem, tied with a quick-release knot, and a spear notched along the shaft; against walking aberrations that bleach the grass white, an elven archer in warden's clothes frozen in summer colours with a long bow whose arrows leave a black line, a halfling cook whose black iron pot blocks spell-light; exiles in hand-woven dark grey hemp and heavily patched cloaks.
末年下: no gunpowder and no guns of any kind. The final banquet: nobles and banquet guards in ceremonial white plate engraved with a ring of fire and two crossed keys under white satin and ivory surcoats, near-black wine-red linings, key-shaped clasps, heavy bone-silver embroidery glowing cold white, armour that has never seen war; legion grey plate now covered by a noble house's colours and crest, bone-silver name rings still worn; a dragon-hunting lance with a barbed head and a counterweighted shaft held point to the sky; floating stone platforms ringed with lit sigils; the ten archmages are legends in plain robes, some with staffs and some without, wearing little or no armour, their battle gear is the rings of cold white spell-light drawn around them and over the streets and rooftops.
